claim: Teaching heuristics alone has a weak human record: Schoenfeld judged in 1982 that there was little conclusive evidence that students learn heuristics and then improve; earlier studies gave single-strategy gains far below hopes.
agent_test: Compare agent with a heuristic list only versus list plus control layer at equal tokens.

claim: Heuristics taught together with a managerial/control strategy lifted human performance: Schoenfeld course group 21 to 73 on the problem test vs 14 to 24 for programming-course control (N 11 vs 8; interaction F(1,17)=48.2). Heuristic and control effects are confounded. Gap search: the 1979 lab study (7 students, all 4 trained beat all 3 controls, p<.05 by rank) also mixed a 5-minute stop-and-review prompt into both arms, and students often failed to use heuristics they knew (d13). No LLM ablation separates heuristics from control; closest is Meta-Reasoner (Game of 24, GPT-4o-mini: full 89, LLM self-selected strategy 82, no controller 4; d04), author-run.
agent_test: Ablate: heuristics only, control only, both; same token budget.

claim: Selecting WHICH technique to use (a selection strategy) beat plain study for integration: strategy group studied 7 h vs 9 h and scored significantly higher (1978, as cited; no statistic). LLM side: Meta-Reasoning Prompting (GPT-4 macro avg 0.772 vs ToT 0.725, CoT 0.654) helps only with a strong model; with GPT-3.5 it falls to 0.433, below SPP 0.469, and GSM8K drops 83.1 to 78.1. Selection accuracy is not reported.
agent_test: Give agent a technique-selection step vs flat technique list.

claim: Student failure is often control, not missing knowledge: in the geometry construction task no pair reasoned to a solution, guessing 15-20 min with tools in hand; pretest 'jump into one approach' was the norm.
agent_test: Count premature-commitment events in agent traces with and without a forced stop-and-assess check.

claim: Classroom heuristic teaching in small modern studies shows gains mostly on easy-to-practise heuristics: auxiliary element use 18% to 74%, kite success 13% to 58% (n=98), but inscribed square 9% to 20%; some heuristics were not teachable.
agent_test: Rank operators by measured gain on held-out problems; keep only those with gain.

claim: Explicit heuristic worked examples raise strategy knowledge, but transfer to modelling competency depends on grade: grade 7 F(2,174)=5.10, grade 5 no effect on modelling (N=134, 180).
agent_test: Add worked examples of heuristic use to agent memory; test by problem difficulty.

claim: A 5-month heuristic-literacy experiment (N=92) reported a moderate mean effect, but coding of 'heuristic' differs across manuals, so counts of heuristic use are not comparable across studies. Measured: three published coding manuals applied to the same 32 actions code 29, 23 and 16 as heuristic (d15).
agent_test: Score agent heuristic use with a fixed written rubric by two raters.

claim: Rival theory: expertise is domain schema knowledge; the authors state no randomized trials show Polya-type strategy teaching improves problem solving, while worked-example trials exist. Counter: Schoenfeld lab and course data and small classroom effects.
agent_test: Equal-token test: heuristic prompt vs domain worked-example retrieval.

claim: Meta-analyses of word-problem instruction show moderate-to-large positive effects (g=0.56 and g=0.71) but pool schema-based and other methods, so they do not isolate heuristic teaching. Hembree (1992) was not opened. Hembree abstract (487 reports): heuristics no better in K-5, mildly better in grades 6-8, distinctly better in high school; effect sizes still not read.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as a prior for effect size.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Generic trigger heuristic works strongly in LLMs: 'Let us think step by step' MultiArith 17.7% to 78.7%, GSM8K 10.4% to 40.7% (text-davinci-002); few-shot CoT PaLM 540B GSM8K 17.9% to 56.9%.
agent_test: Baseline arm: plain CoT; every heuristic must beat it at equal tokens.

claim: CoT-type heuristics help mainly on math, symbolic and logic tasks (mean gains 12.3, 14.2, 6.9 points); little elsewhere. Planning separated from execution adds little; tool execution adds most.
agent_test: Gate heuristic scaffolding by task type; compare to always-on at equal tokens.

claim: Plan-and-solve beats zero-shot CoT only modestly on GSM8K (+2.9; 56.4 to 59.3) and about equals 8-shot CoT on average (76.7 vs 77.6). It trims calculation (7 to 5%) and missing-step (12 to 7%) errors but not semantic misunderstanding (27%). Gains stack with self-consistency (58.7 to 73.7).
agent_test: Run plan-first vs plain at equal tokens; tag errors by type.

claim: Least-to-most (decompose) gives real transfer to harder-than-demonstrated problems on symbolic tasks (SCAN length 99.7% vs CoT 16.2%) but little on GSM8K (62.39 vs 60.87); it is worse on 2-step items (74.53 vs 76.68) and gains only at 5+ steps (45.23 vs 39.07).
agent_test: Trigger decomposition only above a step-count estimate; compare with always-on.

claim: Step-back abstraction helps science and knowledge QA (PaLM-2L Physics 66.4 to 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 to 81.8; GPT-4 Physics 69.4 to 84.5) but gives no edge on GSM8K (84.3 vs 84.4 zero-shot CoT); it fixes 20.5% of baseline errors yet adds 11.9%; over 90% of its errors are in reasoning.
agent_test: Use abstraction on knowledge-heavy items only; measure fixed vs broken.

claim: Self-composed reasoning structures (choose from heuristic modules) beat CoT: BBH PaLM 2-L 60 to 67, GPT-4 75 to 81; MATH gain small (GPT-4 71 to 73). Structures were 87.5% correct yet 74.7% of MATH failures were computation errors, so heuristic choice is not the bottleneck on MATH.
agent_test: Add a module-selection step; check whether computation checks (tool) give more at equal tokens.

claim: Recalling related problems (Polya analogy) matches or slightly beats few-shot CoT: GSM8K GPT-3.5 77.8 vs 75.0/75.8/76.7; MATH 37.3 vs 33.0. In a 100-case audit, generalization gap was the largest single cause among failures with relevant correct recall (12), plus 22 failures from irrelevant or wrong recall.
agent_test: Self-generated exemplars vs fixed exemplars at equal tokens.

claim: Reusing distilled thought templates (Buffer of Thoughts) lifts puzzle tasks at about 12% of multi-query cost: Game of 24 82.4% vs ToT 74.0% vs CoT 11.0%. Gains are largest where a known trick exists.
agent_test: Template library built from solved items; test on held-out items from different families.

claim: Check-your-work heuristics fail without outside signal: GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; GPT-4-Turbo 91.5 to 88.0 to 90.0; GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; with oracle labels GPT-3.5 75.9 to 84.3. Debate does not beat self-consistency at equal responses. Independent support: Stechly 2024 (GPT-4 self-critique Game of 24 5 to 3%; sound verifier 36%; verifier plus plain re-sampling k=25 42%) and the Kamoi 2024 survey (no success from prompted self-feedback outside suitable tasks).
agent_test: Compare self-review pass vs external verifier (tool/test) vs more samples at equal tokens.

claim: Human-like behaviours (verification, backtracking, subgoals, backward chaining) predict RL gains: Qwen ~60% vs Llama ~30% on Countdown; priming Llama with such traces closes the gap; empty-CoT priming stays at 30-35%; wrong-answer traces with the behaviours still work. Transfer to MATH seen only in Qwen (38 to 50%).
agent_test: Test behaviour frequency in traces vs accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Polya-style heuristic diversity in training: up to 64 heuristic variants per question raised average pass@64 from 46.30 to 48.17 and post-RL pass@64 from 44.21 to 47.62; pass@1 gain was small (9.25 to 11.50, below STaR 13.02); incorrect-answer variants fell below vanilla RL; breadth beat depth by about 7% relative.
agent_test: At inference: sample solutions under different heuristics vs same heuristic, equal tokens.

claim: Teaching a fully explicit algorithm in context gives out-of-distribution length generalization where vague hints do not (error about 10x lower on parity, 9x addition).
agent_test: Concrete procedure text vs generic hint for arithmetic-like sub-skills.

claim: Skill-labelled example retrieval beats topic retrieval: MATH +11.6 over standard CoT, +3.5 over topic; GSM8K GPT-4 93.00 to 94.31.
agent_test: Index memory by skill name vs topic.

claim: Cognitive-operation prompts help mid-size open models on GSM8K (hybrid about 95% on LLaMA 70B) but gains shrink for strong models near ceiling. Also MRP selection fails on GPT-3.5 but works on GPT-4 (d02, d03); monitor-and-control gains shrink on a strong base (Gemini-2.0-flash 94.93 to 96.73; d05).
agent_test: Test at several model sizes; expect little gain near ceiling.

claim: Reasoning behaviours can emerge from verifiable-reward RL without taught heuristics; few-shot prompting degraded R1. Measured: on GPQA Diamond, step-by-step prompting changed reasoning models by +0.029, +0.031, -0.033 (d01); decomposition plus token budgets on reasoning models saved tokens with comparable MATH-500 accuracy (d12).
agent_test: Test few-shot heuristic examples on a reasoning-tuned model vs zero-shot.

claim: On reasoning models, generic CoT-style heuristic prompts add near nothing and cost time: GPQA Diamond (4,950 runs per cell) o3-mini +0.029, o4-mini +0.031, Gemini Flash 2.5 -0.033 average rating; richer prompts (decompose, weigh paths) no better. Non-reasoning models gain 0.044 to 0.135 but 3 of 5 get worse on the strict 100%-correct metric.
schema_part: G (do not add heuristic text to reasoning cores)
agent_test: Run the same task set with and without the heuristic block on a reasoning model, report accuracy and tokens, 25 trials.

claim: At equal compute budget, CoT self-consistency matches or beats Plan-and-Solve, Least-to-Most, Progressive-Hint, debate and Reflexion on GPT-3.5 (and GPT-4 except ToT on Game of 24); debate and Reflexion get worse with more budget.
agent_test: Every heuristic arm gets a matched-token plain repeated-attempt arm.

claim: A learned external controller that decides continue, backtrack, switch or restart beats asking the model to choose its own strategy: Game of 24 GPT-4o-mini 89 vs 82 vs 4 (plain CoT); Gemini-Exp 94 vs 87 vs 11. Monitor-and-control roles plus lesson memory lift MATH-500 GPT-4o-mini 72.67 to 85.13, but lesson updates alone reach 80.47.
agent_test: 2x2: heuristics on/off by controller on/off, same tokens; compare LLM self-selection with outcome-driven selection.

claim: Verification pays only with an outside sound signal: GPT-4 self-critique lowers accuracy, a sound verifier raises it, and plain re-sampling under the verifier gets most of the gain (Game of 24 42% at k=25 vs 36% with critique). LLM-as-verifier false negative rate 20.7% (Game of 24) to 97% (Mystery Blocksworld).
agent_test: Compare look-back by the model vs a code or test check vs more samples at equal tokens.

claim: Inference-time heuristic diversity (one sample per model-proposed approach) beats same-prompt resampling at similar cost on GPT-4: graph colouring 97 vs SC-10 23 vs CoT 15; Blocksworld 3 94 vs 73 vs 70; MATH counting +14 to +17 points. No gain for GPT-3.5 on hard planning. No test on reasoning models.
agent_test: Sample k answers under k different heuristics vs k under one, equal tokens, on a reasoning model.

claim: Instruction text placed once drifts: system-prompt compliance decays within about eight dialogue rounds in LLaMA2-70B-chat and GPT-3.5. No test of heuristic persistence exists; human delayed tests are not opened.
agent_test: Drift probe: does the agent still apply the heuristic at step 5, 20, 50 with and without re-injection.

claim: Schoenfeld's 1979 lab study showed what heuristic teaching can and cannot do: cue-driven strategies (induction, fewer variables, diagrams) were learned (3 of 4 vs 1 of 3 on the fewer-variables problem; 4 of 4 vs 0 of 3 on induction), vague ones (subgoals, contradiction) were not, and knowing a strategy did not mean using it.
agent_test: Give each operator an explicit trigger cue; measure use rate when the cue is present.

claim: Prompt-level cross-family transfer of heuristics is untested in LLMs; only training-time transfer is measured, and it is weak for SFT (most math-strong open models fail to transfer to other domains; RL on math transfers).
agent_test: Hold out one problem family per heuristic and measure gain there vs in-family.
